result.topic_en: Euler lists the six possible combinations of end conditions (free, simply fixed, clamped) for a vibrating elastic rod and begins Case I, a rod with both ends free, deriving the boundary equations.

Plures quidem caſus videntur occurrere, veluti ſi E eſſet fixus et F liber; ſed quia ambos terminos inter ſe permutare licet, hic caſus in illis memoratis ſex iam continetur. His igitur poſitis ſex nobis ſuperſunt Problemata, quae breuiter ordine pertractabimus.
Euolutio caſus I.
quo virgae elaſticae vterque terminus prorſus eſt liber.
Problema.
§. 15. Si virga elaſtica a nullis plane viribus ſollicitetur et plano horizontali politiſſimo libere incumbat, inveſtigare omnes vibrationes regulares, quibus ea contremiſcere poteſt.
Solutio.
Quoniam vterque terminus E et F liber aſſumitur, pro vtroque erit tam $(\frac{ddy}{ds^2})=0$ quam $(\frac{d^3 s}{ds^3})=0$, hinc ergo pro termino E poſito $s=0$ naſcuntur hae duae aequationes:
I. $\alpha+\beta-\delta=0$; II. $\alpha-\beta-\gamma=0$;
pro altero termino F erit $s=a$, et poſito breuitatis gratia $\frac{a}{f}=\omega$, iſtae oriuntur aequationes:

items.english: but since the two ends may be interchanged, this case is already contained in the six mentioned.

items.quote: His igitur poſitis ſex nobis ſuperſunt Problemata, quae breuiter ordine pertractabimus.
items.english: With these established, six problems remain for us, which we shall briefly treat in order.

items.quote: Si virga elaſtica a nullis plane viribus ſollicitetur et plano horizontali politiſſimo libere incumbat, inveſtigare omnes vibrationes regulares, quibus ea contremiſcere poteſt.
items.english: If an elastic rod is acted on by no forces at all and lies freely on a perfectly smooth horizontal plane, to investigate all the regular vibrations with which it can vibrate.
